lyrics:
[Intro: lonely piano figure, soft pedal steel]

[Verse 1: female voice, hushed]
Your name's still at the top, I never moved it down
Half a glass of red, quiet house, quiet town
I typed out "you awake?" and I watched it sit
Then I held down the arrow and deleted it

[Chorus: both voices, full band swells]
And I see three dots, then nothing
Three dots, then gone
You're over there typing something
And I'm over here holding on
Say it or don't, I can't take the in-between
Three little dots on a screen

[Verse 2: male voice, low]
I wrote "I'm sorry" and I wrote "I'm fine"
I wrote a whole long paragraph and cut it to a line
I can see you see me, I can see you start
That bubble's got a hold of every piece of my heart

[Chorus: both voices, full band swells]
And I see three dots, then nothing
Three dots, then gone
You're over there typing something
And I'm over here holding on
Say it or don't, I can't take the in-between
Three little dots on a screen

[Bridge: piano only, voices trading]
If you send it, I'll answer
If you answer, I'll drive
Eleven miles of two-lane, and I'm wide awake tonight

[Final Chorus: full band, both voices, then piano alone]
And I see three dots, then nothing
Three dots, then gone
You're over there typing something
And I'm over here holding on
Say it or don't, I can't take the in-between
Three little dots...

[Outro: piano, a message chime, spoken softly]
"Hey."
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 108 BPM, 4/4, E major. A mid-tempo ballad with a ticking pulse, restless and held back.

VOICE: A duet. Female voice first: soft, breathy, close. Male voice second: low and warm. They sing the choruses together in harmony, louder each time. The last line is cut off, and one spoken word follows a chime.

INSTRUMENTS: A repeating piano figure, pedal steel, clean electric guitar, bass, live drums entering at the first chorus, strings in the last chorus, a phone message chime.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, piano. 0:12 Verse 1, her. 0:42 Chorus 1. 1:10 Verse 2, him. 1:40 Chorus 2. 2:08 Bridge, piano only. 2:28 Final chorus, band drops out on the last line. 3:02 Outro, piano, the chime and 'Hey' at 3:30.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-2000s country-pop ballad: polished, wide, piano and voices forward, a big chorus.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The chime and the single spoken 'Hey' at 3:30.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original is a phone call you can hear being dialled. Now the agony is visible: each can watch the other begin to type. And this version lets one of them send it.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Hesitating, watching, aching, one word.
